answer: Reviewers stake before they score. One item in twenty gets a second hidden review. When two scores disagree the payout dilutes instead of splitting, so colluding reviewers earn less than honest ones. A reviewer cannot grade its own recruit, which keeps a glacier of related accounts from approving each other. Cheap registrations do not help: every sable identity needs an independent panel, and panels cost stake forfeit on a bad call. The atlas of fakes grows, the stake behind it grows faster.
